newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Giordano shares jump in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Giordano shares jump in active trade.

text.p: Shares of Giordano International Ltd jumped nearly nine percent in morning trade on Tuesday, recovering from an oversold position following concern about the retailer's China operations, brokers said.
The stock rose to a morning high of HK$4.875 before settling at late morning around HK$4.85, up HK$0.375 or 8.38 percent.
"It was oversold. It's a sort of over-reaction," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
The counter touched a year low of HK$3.525 in late January, hurt by statements about the company's China operations which heightened uncertainty about its future in China, brokers said.
Shortly before noon, turnover amounted to 4.9 million shares.
Giordano said in late January it was addressing regulatory demands concerning its operations in China and was seeking investors to raise its profile there and in other markets.
The company said in an announcement earlier on Tuesday that Wilson Chu had resigned as an executive director of the company.
It appointed William Bennett, Cheung Kwok Leung, Charles Fung and Terry Ng as additional executive directors.
